source.title: PEAR: Position-Embedding-Agnostic Attention Re-weighting Enhances Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Zero Inference Overhead
source.authors: Tao Tan; Yining Qian; Ang Lv; Hongzhan Lin; Songhao Wu; Yong-Bo Wang; Feng Wang; Jing-Tong Wu; Xin Lu; Rui Yan

page_placements.theme: Suppressive attention heads, often working as populations, in other models and tasks

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The study finds heads that suppress copying on a proxy task in other models, but explicitly cautions that these heads need not use the same mechanisms. It therefore refines the scope of the claim about a shared copy-suppression role rather than testing GPT-2 small L10H7 directly.
record.gate_note: The experiments do not use GPT-2 small or test L10H7, its QK/OV circuit, calibration, or self-repair. The study does test proxy-task suppression in three other models. Its RAG benchmark improvements concern the PEAR-reweighted group of heads and do not independently measure copy suppression, so those outcomes are not rows for the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study uses the idea that some heads suppress in-context copying to pick heads for its PEAR re-weighting method, then reports only RAG and MMLU performance. Its Δπ head scores are a selection step: the authors pick the top K heads by Δπ. They never check whether those heads perform copy suppression in the McDougall sense (QK/OV, suppressing predicted in-context tokens across the distribution). Section 4.1 says Section 5.6 shows the heads 'may serve various functions, such as copy suppression'. Section 5.6 shows no such analysis, only a speculative explanation of learned τ values. No version is tested, so no verdicts are given.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that PEAR improves RAG and MDQA performance with zero inference overhead across different position embeddings, without hurting MMLU. It works by re-weighting heads chosen on a copying proxy task. They state the heads need not share one mechanism. Their claim that Section 5.6 shows varied functions, including copy suppression, is not backed by any analysis in that section; it only offers a 'plausible explanation' for τ values above 1.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a random-token copying proxy and path patching to select heads in Llama2, OPT, and Baichuan, then learns reweighting coefficients. It does not reproduce the GPT-2 small L10H7 QK/OV analysis or its loss attribution.
record.method_sensitivity: The number of selected heads K affects results: for Llama2-7B-chat, the authors report best performance at K=30 and worse results when K is smaller or larger.

fits_no_version.finding: In Llama2-7B-chat, OPT-6.7B and Baichuan-13B-chat, a distinct group of heads (30, 22 and 21) raises the logit of the expected copied token when mean-ablated at position 2n−1 on repeated random-token sequences. Values appear only in heatmaps (Fig. 3, 5–7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger LLMs contain a small group of heads that suppress induction-style copying on repeated random tokens, whatever their mechanism.

record.problems: The paper does not report individual numerical Δπ values in text; the head-score evidence is shown in heatmaps. Discovered heads are not mechanistically characterized individually, and PEAR reweights a selected group rather than isolating each head's downstream effect.
record.rows_left_out: No results relevant to the claim were omitted. RAG benchmark scores and MMLU results are not rows because they do not directly measure the copy-suppression behavior or shared mechanism named by V5.

untested.parts: GPT-2 small L10H7 is not studied.
No QK/OV circuit analysis and no loss attribution.
No upstream-copier ablation and no self-repair measurement.
Whether the heads found in Llama2, OPT and Baichuan are copy-suppression heads. The authors explicitly leave each head's mechanism for future work.

record.verdict_notes: The record's reader labelled this T5/tests with a V5 limits_scope verdict. That is not supported: the authors' caution about differing mechanisms is an unverified disclaimer, not a result. Δπ scores are used to select heads for the method. The peer-review field ('The Web Conference, 2024') is not stated in the text, which is an arXiv preprint.

versions.untested_parts: GPT-2 small L10H7 and its main role across the training distribution.
The QK and OV circuits and their contribution to loss, including the 76.9% figure.
Calibration and overconfidence from naive copying.
Self-repair following ablation of an upstream copier.

Whether the specific negative name movers in IOI, or the GPT-2 small head, share the same mechanism as any discovered heads; the paper does not analyze the individual mechanisms of its discovered heads.
The distribution-wide contribution of copy suppression versus other self-repair mechanisms.

rows.subject: Llama2-7B-chat-4k
rows.operation_detail: At position 2n−1, replace an individual head's output with its mean output over the sequence; measure the change in the expected copied token's logit.

conditions.value: 10, 15, 25, 50; final head scores average repeated experiments

rows.measure: Δπ, defined as the intervened-to-normal logit ratio for the expected token minus 1
rows.value: The authors report a group of heads with significantly large Δπ values and select the top K=30; individual Δπ values are not stated in text.
rows.note: Table 2 lists the selected heads. The study treats the selected heads as suppressing performance on the copying proxy task; it does not establish that they share a specific mechanism.
rows.check: Selection values for the study's own method (top-K heads by Δπ), shown only in heatmaps. The study does not measure whether these heads perform copy suppression or share L10H7's role, so the row cannot bear on V5. The ablation is mean over sequence positions at position 2n−1 only. Δπ is a logit ratio on repeated random tokens, not the copy-suppression behaviour across the distribution.

relation.reason: Applies the finding to head selection and reweighting, while explicitly leaving characterization of individual heads' mechanisms to future work.

tranche.reason: Uses suppression of contextual copying to motivate PEAR; Δπ scores select heads for the method. Downstream performance and learned coefficients do not establish the copy-suppression mechanism or any claim version.

source_check.notes: The text states the selected group sizes and qualitative Δπ findings; individual scores appear only in heatmaps. Section 5.6 analyzes learned coefficients, without demonstrating which heads implement copy suppression.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: The three tested models on the random-token copying proxy task
reader_labels.reason: The proxy-task results identify suppressive heads in all three models, but the authors caution that RAG-suppression heads can have different functions and do not imply a shared mechanism; see r1–r3.
